title: Normalization of the specified coefficient ringed-square comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$, and a $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $a:R\to S$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings such that $\operatorname{Ext}_{a_Z}$ is exact for every scheme $Z$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. On ordinary unbounded derived categories of internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] put $T_Z=L\operatorname{Ext}_{a_Z}$, $U_Z=D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_Z})$, $P_R=Lf_R^*$, $G_R=Rf_{R*}$, and similarly $P_S,G_S$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Take the small pro-etale sites small relative to the module-sheaf universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Write $E_{R,Z},E_{S,Z}$ for the fixed internal-module/section-module equivalences [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison, lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction], and use their specified derived operation and adjunction identifications. The section-ring coefficient maps define identity-underlying-topos morphisms $\phi_Z:(Z,S_Z)\to(Z,R_Z)$ and geometric ringed-topos morphisms $f_R,f_S$. Their coefficient square commutes with identity underlying commutation. Let $\theta:P_ST_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}T_XP_R$ and $C:G_RU_X\xrightarrow{\sim}U_YG_S$ denote, after these identifications, the canonical ringed pullback and direct-image path comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction], with ringed paths $f_R\circ\phi_X$ and $\phi_Y\circ f_S$ respectively.
Let $e:U_YG_S\xrightarrow{\sim}G_RU_X$ be the specified restriction/direct-image comparison [def-sfb-derived-comap-lower-star-iso], and $c:T_XP_R\xrightarrow{\sim}P_ST_Y$ its specified conjugate [def-sfb-derived-pull-iso]. Then $C=e^{-1}$ and $\theta=c^{-1}$ as natural transformations between these actual derived functors. More precisely, if $I$ is a K-injective complex [def-pur-kinjective-complex] of $S_X$-module sheaves and $Q$ is localization, then under the canonical resolution identifications $C_{QI}=Q(\vartheta_I^{-1})$ and $e_{QI}=Q(\vartheta_I)$, where $\vartheta:\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y}f_{S*}\cong f_{R*}\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}$ is the identity-on-underlying-sheaves comparison [def-sfb-comap-lower-star-iso]. The equality $\theta=c^{-1}$ concerns the comparison conjugate to these specified direct-image composition maps, rather than an arbitrarily chosen pullback isomorphism.

proof.text: Expand C and e and use the preceding equality for exact postcomposition. Their four factors are inverse factors in reverse order, including the inverse ordinary coefficient bridge. Thus C=e.symm as natural isomorphisms. The definitions of the pullback comparison and derivedPullIso are inverse conjugates along the same two composite adjunctions. The inverse-component formula of conjugateIsoEquiv gives theta=c.symm.

proof.text: Evaluate the universal-unit equation for the derived natural transformation of comapLowerStarIso on a K-injective I. Evaluate both composition-unit equations there. The source restriction preserves K-injectivity, so its resolution comparison is the inverse unit. The target exact-factorization comparison cancels with the exact-restriction derived-unit comparison by hom_fac. Substitute the two composition equations into the derived bridge equation; cancel the inverse resolution units. This proves targetResolution.inv followed by e followed by sourceResolution.hom equals Q of the ordinary bridge. The private objQ and factorsh helpers only normalize the canonical homotopy/complex localization identifications. No K-injectivity of the geometric pushforward of I is assumed.
